label: On brief
description: Is the draft about what the brief asks, for the reader it names? Judged apart from how well it's written.

label: Argument
description: Is the main point clear, and does the draft make the case for it?

label: Evidence
description: Are the claims backed by sources, examples or figures that actually fit them?

label: Development
description: Is there enough on-topic material to earn the main point?

label: Straight talk
description: Free of padding, vague words, repetition and claims stated more strongly than shown.

label: Structure
description: Does each part follow from the last, with clear turns between them?

label: Rhythm
description: Do sentence lengths vary enough to keep the reader moving?

label: Voice
description: Does it sound like one writer, pitched at the reader the brief names?

label: Word choice
description: Precise, varied words rather than repeats, abstractions and jargon.

label: Paragraphs
description: A readable mix of short and long paragraphs, each doing one job.

label: Reader pull
description: Would the reader stay to the end? Follows the overall grade rather than being marked on its own.
